ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Low ratio of high-intensity pixels to low-intensity pixels; approximately 15:85 white-to-black distribution across the visible ventral fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant low-intensity dark pigmentation (black/dark grey) across >85% of fluke area. High-intensity white linear clusters (scratches) mapped across the medial and lateral regions. High-contrast white and reddish-brown contiguous blobs mapped at the distal tips of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression; approximately 45-degree angle at the vertex with a high depth-to-width ratio within the bounding box of the lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Extremely irregular topography. Left lobe trailing edge displays high-amplitude, high-frequency jagged variations (broken profile). Right lobe trailing edge displays lower-amplitude, moderate-frequency serrations.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Left lobe exhibits a truncated and irregular convexity. Right lobe exhibits a long, slender trajectory with a distinct mid-axis concavity transitioning to terminal convexity.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Large, dense clusters of high-contrast white and off-white pixels at the distal tips of both lobes (barnacle colonization). Smaller, isolated white circular pixel clusters are visible across the central-left lobe body.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Numerous unaligned white linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) are clearly visible, primarily oriented diagonally across the dark pigmentation of both lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Significant morphological trauma/amputation at the tip of the left lobe; presence of large white and reddish biological encrustations at both distal extremities.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique reddish-brown pixel clusters mixed with white at the terminal end of the left lobe, distinct from typical fluke pigmentation.
